shipped_row.boundary_rationale:
This admonition spans the whole zone as one imperative/jussive-framed unit. The zone's directive forms cluster at its two ends: שַׁלַּ֥ח (oshb:Eccl.11.1, tier: byte), "send", opens the counsel, matching “Cast your bread on the waters” (web:Eccl.11.1); תֶּן (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte), "give", continues it, matching “Give a portion to seven, yes, even to eight” (web:Eccl.11.2); and the unit closes with זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "sow", paired with the negative אַל תַּנַּ֣ח (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), "do not let...rest", matching “In the morning sow your seed...in the evening don't withhold your hand” (web:Eccl.11.6). The three middle verses carry no second-person directive at all: v.3 opens a conditional protasis, אִם...עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte); v.4 is a participial clause with a negated prefix-conjugation, שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte); and v.5 is a comparative declarative. This directive distribution, imperatives at the frame's two ends bracketing a directive-free middle, is what fixes the unit's own bounds rather than any split within it.

Three byte-grounded binders carry across the zone's internal seams. The negated-knowledge refrain interlocks the opening, middle and close: לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) collates at accent-stripped tier against כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte), and אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte) collates at skeleton tier against אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte); each attested form is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the know-negation, web:Eccl.11.2 and web:Eccl.11.5; sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the negated-existential form, web:Eccl.11.5 and web:Eccl.11.6), with all four sites falling inside this unit. The seam at 11:2/11:3 itself carries a repeated phrase, עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) against עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte), word-bound at skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, and 11:2/11:3 the only adjacent pair among them). A third binder ties the declarative middle to the closing imperative: the same triliteral sowing root (ז-ר-ע) stands in יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte) and in זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), different inflected forms of the one root, not a word-bound identity, but book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside it). No byte warrant separates any internal seam that these three binders do not themselves cross.

Both outer bounds hold clean on content rather than chapter numbering: the back seam shares with the preceding verse only a causal particle, a function word, and that verse closes its own sentence zone (web:Eccl.10.20); the forward seam shares with the following verse only the object marker, and that verse opens the light-frame that begins the aging-allegory zone (web:Eccl.11.7).

The three middle verses carry no second-person directive at all: v.3 opens a conditional protasis, אִם...עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte); v.4 is a participial clause with a negated prefix-conjugation, שֹׁמֵ֥ר ר֖וּחַ לֹ֣א יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte); and v.5 is a comparative declarative. This directive distribution, imperatives at the frame's two ends bracketing a directive-free middle, is what fixes the unit's own bounds rather than any split within it.

Three byte-grounded binders carry across the zone's internal seams. The negated-knowledge refrain interlocks the opening, middle and close: לֹ֣א תֵדַ֔ע (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) collates at accent-stripped tier against כָּ֗כָה לֹ֤א תֵדַע֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte), and אֵֽינְךָ֤ יוֹדֵ֨עַ֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.5, tier: byte) collates at skeleton tier against אֵֽינְךָ֨ יוֹדֵ֜ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte); each attested form is book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the know-negation, web:Eccl.11.2 and web:Eccl.11.5; sweep: 2 verses book-wide for the negated-existential form, web:Eccl.11.5 and web:Eccl.11.6), with all four sites falling inside this unit. The seam at 11:2/11:3 itself carries a repeated phrase, עַל הָאָֽרֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.2, tier: byte) against עַל הָאָ֣רֶץ (oshb:Eccl.11.3, tier: byte), word-bound at skeleton tier (sweep: 7 verses book-wide, and 11:2/11:3 the only adjacent pair among them). A third binder ties the declarative middle to the closing imperative: the same triliteral sowing root (ז-ר-ע) stands in יִזְרָ֑ע (oshb:Eccl.11.4, tier: byte) and in זְרַ֣ע (oshb:Eccl.11.6, tier: byte), different inflected forms of the one root, not a word-bound identity, but book-exclusive to this span (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, both inside it). No byte warrant separates any internal seam that these three binders do not themselves cross.

Both outer bounds hold clean on content rather than chapter numbering: the back seam shares with the preceding verse only a causal particle, a function word, and that verse closes its own sentence zone (web:Eccl.10.20); the forward seam shares with the following verse only the object marker, and that verse opens the light-frame that begins the aging-allegory zone (web:Eccl.11.7).

next_row.boundary_rationale: The aging-allegory poem is spined by a triple anaphora, spliced at each site: עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹא (oshb:Eccl.12.1, tier: byte) — "before...not" — עַ֠ד אֲשֶׁ֨ר לֹֽא (oshb:Eccl.12.2, tier: byte), and עַ֣ד אֲשֶׁ֤ר לֹֽא (oshb:Eccl.12.6, tier: byte), all matching the identical skeleton phrase, framing “before the evil days come” (web:Eccl.12.1), “Before the sun, the light, the moon, and the stars are darkened” (web:Eccl.12.2), and “before the silver cord is severed” (web:Eccl.12.6). This poem is held to open at v.1 rather than at the wider zone's own possible start at 11:9, because the unbroken 2ms-imperative chain crossing into this unit — שְׂמַ֧ח (oshb:Eccl.11.9), וְהָסֵ֥ר (oshb:Eccl.11.10), וּזְכֹר֙ (oshb:Eccl.12.1) — together with the youth-phrase catchword (בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Eccl.11.9) against בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Eccl.12.1), sweep: 2 verses) is disclosed rather than treated as decisive: the imperative chain and catchword continue across the seam, but v.1's own address shifts from the youth-in-general counsel of 11:9-10 to the more specific creator-remembrance charge that spines this poem's own anaphora, so the boundary is held here rather than moved. V.6 also carries an inline ketiv/qere pair on two distinct roots rather than one lexeme pointed two ways: the ketiv ירחק (root ר-ח-ק, "be far/removed") against the qere יֵרָתֵק֙ (oshb:Eccl.12.6, ketiv/qere; tier: byte; root ר-ת-ק, "be loosed/snapped"), an openly-held crux over which sense the clause carries. The poem's theological terminus is spliced whole as וְיָשֹׁ֧ב הֶעָפָ֛ר עַל הָאָ֖רֶץ כְּשֶׁהָיָ֑ה וְהָר֣וּחַ תָּשׁ֔וּב אֶל הָאֱלֹהִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר נְתָנָֽהּ (oshb:Eccl.12.7, tier: byte) — "the dust returns to the earth as it was, and the spirit returns to God" — matching “the spirit returns to God who gave it” (web:Eccl.12.7), closing the monologue parent immediately before the plene-definite motto that opens the epilogue frame.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the poem into three smaller rows at the three anaphora sites (v.1-2, v.3-5, v.6-7) is rejected because the anaphora functions as the poem's own internal spine rather than three independently-closed units, matching how the time-catalogue's internal repetition is held as one list unit.

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The bridge opens in third-person reflection, “Truly the light is sweet” (web:Eccl.11.7), turning at v.8 to a conditional: כִּ֣י אִם שָׁנִ֥ים הַרְבֵּ֛ה יִחְיֶ֥ה הָאָדָ֖ם (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) — "if a man lives many years" — followed by its own apodosis, בְּכֻלָּ֣ם יִשְׂמָ֑ח (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) — “let him rejoice in them all” (web:Eccl.11.8), and its own remember-clause, וְיִזְכֹּר֙ (oshb:Eccl.11.8, tier: byte) — "and let him remember" — matching “let him remember the days of darkness” (web:Eccl.11.8). At v.9 the register shifts to direct second-person vocative address, spliced as שְׂמַ֧ח בָּח֣וּר (oshb:Eccl.11.9, tier: byte) — "rejoice, young man" — matching “Rejoice, young man, in your youth” (web:Eccl.11.9). Both halves are held as one row because the rejoice root recurs at v.8 and v.9 (though the remember root stands at 1 of 4 verses in the span, v.8, not repeated at v.9-10), continuing without a discourse-frame break; the 3rd-to-2nd-person shift at v.8/9 is disclosed as a live alternative seam. An unbroken 2ms-imperative chain — שְׂמַ֧ח (oshb:Eccl.11.9) here, וְהָסֵ֥ר (oshb:Eccl.11.10) in the verse that follows, and וּזְכֹר֙ (oshb:Eccl.12.1) in the unit after that — together with the near-identical youth-phrase catchword (בִּימֵ֣י בְחוּרוֹתֶ֔ךָ (oshb:Eccl.11.9) against בִּימֵ֖י בְּחוּרֹתֶ֑יךָ (oshb:Eccl.12.1), sweep: 2 verses) both cross this unit's own closing seam into the poem that follows; the row still closes at v.10 because the register there completes the youth-address begun at v.9, while the imperative chain's continuation into the poem is disclosed as cross-seam texture rather than adopted as a boundary shift. The unit closes on “youth and the dawn of life are vanity” (web:Eccl.11.10), immediately before the aging-allegory poem's own imperative opens.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting v.7-8 (third-person reflection) from v.9-10 (direct youth address) at the person-register shift is a live alternative, disclosed rather than adopted, because the rejoice root continues across the shift without an intervening discourse frame.

The qohelet-name form here, spliced as הַקּוֹהֶ֖לֶת (oshb:Eccl.12.8, tier: byte), is the plene definite spelling, the sole plene site among the name’s seven occurrences (sweep: 7 verses; the other six are the defective spelling). The havel-havalim superlative phrase spliced as הֲבֵ֧ל הֲבָלִ֛ים (oshb:Eccl.12.8, tier: byte) brackets the monologue with its opening occurrence at the row-external verse Eccl.1.2 (sweep: 2 verses), forming the book’s own inclusio. This tier-1 frame-vocabulary shift (defective spelling everywhere else, plene definite spelling at this one site among the seven, sweep: 7 verses) is the boundary evidence separating the motto from the monologue that precedes it.
